question: The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha, which was one of the strongest political organisations of 19th century India in Maharashtra, was launched in the year:
solution:
The correct answer is __**1870**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha was one of the earliest political organizations in India and was founded in 1870.
 
• It played a significant role in the political awakening and social reforms in Maharashtra during the 19th century.
 
• Many prominent leaders of Indian National Congress like Bal Gangadhar Tilak were associated with this Sabha.
 
• The organization was instrumental in laying the groundwork for the Indian freedom struggle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Poona Sarvajanik Sabha:**

 
 
• Founded in 1870, the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha was one of the early political organizations in British India.
 
• The Sabha aimed at addressing public grievances and representing Indian interests to the British authorities.
 
• It was established by Mahadev Govind Ranade, S. H. Chiplunkar, Ganesh Vasudeo Joshi, and other social reformers.
 
• The Sabha played a crucial role in mobilizing public opinion against the British rule and was a precursor to the Indian National Congress.
 
 
 
• **19th Century Political Organizations in India:**
 
 
• Several political organizations were formed in the 19th century which laid the foundation for the Indian independence movement.
 
• The Indian National Congress (INC) was founded in 1885 and became a major force in the fight against British colonial rule.
 
• Other significant organizations included the Indian Association (1876) and the Bombay Presidency Association (1885).
 
• These organizations were instrumental in raising political consciousness and advocating for reforms and self-governance.
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra's Role in Indian Freedom Struggle:**
 
 
• Maharashtra was a key region in the Indian freedom struggle with several prominent leaders emerging from this state.
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Gopal Krishna Gokhale, and Vinayak Damodar Savarkar were among the notable freedom fighters from Maharashtra.
 
• The region saw significant activities related to the Swadeshi movement, non-cooperation movement, and civil disobedience movement.
 
• The contributions of Maharashtra to the Indian independence movement were profound and enduring.
